title: riemstats
text: Modern neuroimaging studies often collect brain connectivity data across multiple sites increase sample size generalizability. However, introduces significant challenges associated fact different scanners, protocols, populations introduce systematic biases. Traditional statistical methods fail address challenges simultaneously, either ignoring geometric structure SPD matrices lacking appropriate harmonization capabilities.

title: riemstats
text: riemstats addresses challenges two complementary sets tools: Harmonization Methods: Remove unwanted site/scanner effects preserving biological signals ComBat harmonization adapted SPD matrices (see Honorro et al.) Rigid geometric alignment methods (see Simeon et al.) ANOVA Methods: Test group differences respecting SPD geometry Fréchet ANOVA using Riemannian distances (see Muller et al.) Wilks’ lambda Pillai’s trace statistics tangent space Bootstrap inference robust significance testing integrating harmonization ANOVA within Riemannian framework, riemstats enables rigorous statistical analysis multi-site connectome data preserving geometric properties make matrices meaningful representations brain connectivity.

code: library(riemstats) library(riemtan) # Required for CSuperSample and CSample classes #>  #> Attaching package: 'riemtan' #> The following object is masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     dexp data("airm")  # Load the AIRM metric  # Create example SPD matrices for demonstration test_pd_mats <- list(   Matrix::Matrix(c(2.0, 0.5, 0.5, 3.0), nrow = 2) |>     Matrix::nearPD() |> _$mat |> Matrix::pack(),   Matrix::Matrix(c(1.5, 0.3, 0.3, 2.5), nrow = 2) |>     Matrix::nearPD() |> _$mat |> Matrix::pack() )  # Create samples for two sites/groups sample1 <- test_pd_mats |>   purrr::map(\(x) (2 * x) |> Matrix::unpack() |> as("dpoMatrix") |> Matrix::pack()) |>   CSample$new(metric_obj = airm) sample2 <- test_pd_mats |> CSample$new(metric_obj = airm)  # Combine into a supersample for analysis super_sample <- list(sample1, sample2) |> CSuperSample$new()

# Fréchet ANOVA for overall group differences # Returns p-value directly frechet_p_value <- frechet_anova(super_sample)  # Riemannian ANOVA with permutation test inference # Can use log_wilks_lambda (default) or pillais_trace as stat_fun riemann_p_value_wilks <- riem_anova(   ss = super_sample,   stat_fun = log_wilks_lambda,   nperm = 100 # Number of permutations (use 1000+ in practice) )  # Using Pillai's trace riemann_p_value_pillai <- riem_anova(   ss = super_sample,   stat_fun = pillais_trace,   nperm = 100 # Number of permutations (use 1000+ in practice) )  # Display results cat("Fréchet ANOVA p-value:", frechet_p_value, "

title: riemstats 0.2.0
text: Function parameter renamed: den → nperm (default changed 5 1000) Old function one_bootstrap() removed replaced one_permutation() Users must update existing code use new parameter name Benefits permutation test approach: - Faster computation (synthetic data generation required) - stable p-values (parameter estimation variability) - Exact test null hypothesis (group labels exchangeable) - Simpler implementation (direct shuffling observations) Motivation: - Asymptotic tests showed inflation issues - Bootstrap computationally expensive -conservative - Permutation test natural comparing sub-populations See GitHub issue #61 PR #62 detailed discussion implementation.
